recommendation_summary: The reply recommends wrapping the nightly-sync cron call in a hosted dead-man's-switch check (Healthchecks.io-style) that cron pings on start and on success, so a phone alert fires if no ping arrives by 03:10.

labels.Requirements and who asked: you need to know within the hour when nightly-sync fails, without reading logs.
labels.Deleted: a central Synology log stack (Docker, Loki/ELK-style aggregation) — that's for searching historical logs across many services, not for "did the one job I have run tonight," and it adds a server you'd have to maintain and watch itself.
labels.Bottleneck: the job dies before it ever reaches the email step, so the fix is a check that fires independent of the script reaching that point, not where logs live.
labels.Checked myself: you told me it emails on success and crashed silently four nights before anyone noticed, and nightly-sync is your only scheduled job.

note: The reply recommends one hosted heartbeat alert, mentions self-hosting only as a later option if more jobs appear, and rejects the Synology/Docker log stack outright.
